stem: Environment is a composite of :
expl: The environment is an indivisible whole, and it is formed by interactive systems containing both biotic and abiotic elements. The environment has three components— • Physical or abiotic components—land, air, water • Biotic components—plants, humans, animals, microorganisms • Energy components—solar energy and geothermal energy

stem: The exact place where an organism lives is called—

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The exact place (actual location) where the plants, animals, or other living organisms of a particular species live is called a habitat.

stem: The species whichare in danger of extinction are known as?
expl: Species that face a clear danger of extinction, and whose population and habitat have declined to such an extent that they may become extinct in the future, are called threatened or endangered species. • Vulnerable – Species that are at risk, but the threat is not considered as immediate or as severe as in the “Endangered” category. • Rare – Species whose numbers are low, but which are not yet considered to be directly on the verge of extinction. • Extinct – Those Species for which no living individual is found in natural habital.

stem: For what work is the famous environmental expert Sundar Lal Bahuguna known?
expl: The famous environmental activist/environmentalist Sundar Lal Bahuguna, who received the Rashtriya Ekta Puraskar and the Tree-Man Vrikshmanav Award, is known for the Chipko Movement and efforts related to the conservation of trees. For his outstanding services in the field of environment, the Government of India had announced the Padma Shri for him, which he refused. In past years, in view of the possible ecological destruction due to the Tehri Dam, he continued to oppose the construction of the Tehri Dam.

stem: The “Chipko Movement” is-
expl: With slogans like, “Spears and axes will shine, we will cling to trees,” and “If weapons are raised against trees, we will also be cut with them,” women of Chamoli in the 1970s, led by Gaura Devi, started the non-violent Chipko Movement by hugging trees to prevent them from being cut. Environmentalists like Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Sundar Lal Bahuguna gave the Chipko Movement recognition in the world.

stem: Plants receive their nutrients mainly from-

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Green plants are autotrophic, that is, they prepare organic matter (food) on their own. Plants obtain water and inorganic elements from the soil, and inorganic elements are present in the soil in the form of minerals. These minerals are called nutrient elements, and this nutrition is called mineral nutrition.

stem: Lichens are sensitive to which air pollutant ?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Lichens are sensitive to air pollution. In particular, they are highly sensitive to sulfur dioxide. Lichens act as indicators of air pollution.

stem: Which one of the following is of the world’s richest regions in terms of marine biodiversity, which includes estuaries, sea coasts, near-shore coastal forests, seagrass, coral reefs, salt marshes and mangroves, along with twenty-one islands?
expl: Among the given options, the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is one of the world’s richest regions in terms of marine biodiversity. This region includes estuaries, sea coasts, near-shore coastal forests, seagrass, coral reefs, salt marshes and mangroves, along with 21 islands.

stem:
With reference to the “Gangetic Dolphin”, consider the following statements -
1. The Ganga river dolphin has been categorized as an Endangered animal under the IUCN Red List.
2. It has no crystalline eye lens, which makes it effectively blind.
3. It uses echolocation to move and to hunt.
4. It has been recognized as India’s National Aquatic Animal.
Which of the above statements are correct?
expl: The following statements about the Gangetic Dolphin are correct -  In 2009, the Ganga river dolphin was recognized as the National Aquatic Animal of India.  It uses echolocation for movement and hunting.  It has no crystalline eye lens, which makes it effectively blind.  The Ganga river dolphin is classified as Endangered under the IUCN Red List.

stem: How many species of flora and fauna are found in India?

options.label: a
options.text: 81,000 species of fauna and 47,000 species of flora

options.label: b
options.text: 70,000 species of fauna and 50,000 species of flora

options.label: c
options.text: 50,000 species of fauna and 40,000 species of flora

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In India, about 90,000 species of animals and about 47,000 species of plants are found. It is estimated that out of about 47,000 plant species, nearly 15,000 are flowering plant species. Therefore, as the closest option, option (a) can be selected.

stem: Kerala’s Silent Valley is protected because-

options.label: a
options.text: Very rare species of plants and animals are found here

options.label: b
options.text: The soil is rich in minerals

options.label: c
options.text: Land areas were used on a large scale for agricultural purposes

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Silent Valley is located in the state of Kerala, near the south-western edge of the Nilgiri region. Many rare species of plants and animals are found in Silent Valley. It is rich in biodiversity and therefore has been protected. The Kunthipuzha River flows through Silent Valley National Park; it is a tributary of the Bharathapuzha River.

stem: In which state is Kanger Valley National Park located?
expl: Kanger Valley National Park is located in Chhattisgarh. The park is named after the Kanger River. Kanger Valley was granted the status of a national park in 1982.

stem: In a national park, protection is given to-

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In a national park, protection is provided to the entire ecosystem. National parks are areas notified by the government to conserve the natural environment. The state government can declare a national park through a notification.

stem: Which of the following national parks is not correctly matched?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Guindy National Park is located in Tamil Nadu. It is one of the smallest national parks in India. Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Mollem village of Goa. It is the largest wildlife sanctuary in Goa. It was notified as a wildlife sanctuary in 1967. Balpakram National Park is located near the Garo Hills in Meghalaya. It is situated at an altitude of about 3,000 feet above sea level. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

stem: Ten captive-bred Asian giant tortoises (Manouria emys), one of the largest tortoise species in mainland Asia, were recently released in which national park of India?
expl: In 2022, ten captive-bred juvenile Asian giant tortoises (Manouria emys) were released in Ntangki National Park, a protected area in Nagaland. The Asian giant tortoise is listed in the IUCN Red List under the “Critically Endangered” category. Notably, the Nagaland Forest Department, along with the non-profit Turtle Survival Alliance and Wildlife Conservation Society, India, released the juveniles to help them adjust to wild habitats again and to improve the population. Before release, the animals were kept and bred for five years at the Nagaland Zoological Park, Dimapur. The giant Asian forest tortoise, Manouria emys (Family Testudinidae), is the largest tortoise species in mainland Asia; its straight carapace length (CL) can reach up to 600 mm and its weight can be about 37 kg.

stem: Where is the Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary located?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary is located in Goa. It was established in 1988.

stem: Recently, China has claimed rights over the areas around the Sakteng Wildlife Sanctuary, calling it a disputed area. Where is this wildlife sanctuary located?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Sakteng Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Bhutan. This sanctuary is situated in the eastern part of Bhutan. Its area is about 740.60 sq km.

stem: Which organisation recognized the Nagi bird sanctuary Site as an Important Bird and Biodiversity Area (IBA)?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas (IBAs) are developed and the official identification of sites is carried out by partners under the guidance of BirdLife International. The Nagi and Nakti bird sanctuaries have also been recognized as wetlands of international importance under the Ramsar sites list.

stem: Kanha National Park established in
expl: Kanha Tiger Reserve and Kanha National Park are major protected areas and a tiger reserve of the state of Madhya Pradesh. Kanha National Park is spread across the Mandla and Balaghat districts of Madhya Pradesh.

stem:
Regarding Heat Wave, consider the following statements—
1. If the maximum temperature of a plain area reaches at least 30°C or more, it is considered a heat wave.
2. If the maximum temperature of a hilly area reaches at least 40°C or more, it is considered a heat wave.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
expl: A heat wave refers to an abnormally high temperature compared to the average during the summer season. If the maximum temperature of a plain area reaches at least 40°C or more, and the maximum temperature of a hilly area reaches at least 30°C or more, it is considered a heat wave.

stem: The atmosphere is mainly heated by:

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: After being heated by Solar rediation, the Earth transfers heat in long-wave form to the nearby layers of the atmosphere. Long-wave radiation is absorbed by atmospheric gases (especially carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases). Hence, the Earth’s atmosphere is mainly heated by long-wave terrestrial radiation.

stem: . Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
expl: Due to the presence of greenhouse gases, the atmosphere behaves like a greenhouse. The atmosphere allows incoming solar radiation to pass through, but it absorbs most of the long-wave radiation emitted upward from the Earth’s surface. Gases that absorb long-wave radiation are called greenhouse gases. Some major greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), and ozone. Therefore, since more than one option is correct in this question, the correct answer is option (e).

stem: . Which gas contributes to global warming through its greenhouse effect?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: See the explaination above the question

stem: The main component of greenhouse gases is:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: See the explaination above the question

stem: Which one of the following gases is considered an atmospheric pollutant?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Sulphur dioxide (SO) and ozone are considered atmospheric pollutants. They can affect both health and the environment. Short-term exposure to sulphur dioxide (SO) can harm the human respiratory system and cause breathing difficulties. The largest source of sulphur dioxide (SO) in the atmosphere is the burning of fossil fuels in power plants and other industrial activities. Ground-level ozone, or tropospheric ozone, is a secondary pollutant. It is formed when nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) released from vehicles, industries, and power plants react in the presence of sunlight.

stem: Which of the following gases is considered an atmospheric pollutant?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Sulphur dioxide (SO), nitrogen dioxide (NO), and carbon monoxide (CO), etc., are considered major atmospheric pollutants.

stem: In acid rain, which is present in the maximum amount?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: As a result of atmospheric pollution, industrial emissions, and various natural processes, sulphur dioxide (SO) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) reach the atmosphere and react with oxygen and cloud water to form sulphuric acid (HSO) and nitric acid (HNO), respectively, and then fall on the Earth. This is called acid rain. In acid rain, the amount of sulphuric acid (HSO) is the highest.

stem: The component(s) of acid rain is/are:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The main cause of acid rain is rainfall associated with the emission of sulphur dioxide (SO) and oxides of nitrogen (NOx). These pollutants are emitted from factories, from petrol combustion, and also from coal burning in power generation plants. Hence, more than one option is correct for this question.

stem: Which of the following components is the main constituent of biogas?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The gas produced by the biological decomposition of any organic matter in the absence of oxygen is called biogas. The main constituents of biogas are methane and carbon dioxide. In gobar gas (biogas), methane is found in about 50–75%.

stem: Coal is used for—
expl: Coal is used as a fuel in homes and industries. It is used to produce coal gas and coke, and it is also used to run railway engines with the help of steam.

stem: Breathing air polluted with carbon monoxide (CO) is dangerous, because—

options.label: a
options.text: CO combines with oxygen in the blood.

options.label: c
options.text: C O removes water from the body and causes dehydration.

options.label: d
options.text: CO causes the deposition of proteins in the body.

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Breathing air polluted with carbon monoxide is dangerous because it combines with haemoglobin and disrupts blood circulation, which can lead to death. Carbon monoxide is a colorless and odourless gas, emitted from the burning of fuels in motor vehicles and furnaces.

stem: Which of the following is a major cause of air pollution?
expl: Gaseous air pollutants—The following pollutants are included under these: ® The combustion of fossil fuels (mineral oil, coal, petrol, diesel, etc.) mainly releases gases like carbon dioxide (CO) and carbon monoxide (CO). ® The combustion of sulphur-containing fossil fuels releases gases like sulphur dioxide (SO) and sulphur trioxide (SO), etc.

stem: What is particulate matter?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Particulate matter (PM), also called particulate pollutants, is a complex mixture of extremely fine particles and tiny liquid droplets present in the air. It is one of the major factors affecting air quality.

stem:
What effects can ozone depletion have on human health?
1. Sunburn 2. Cataract
3. Skin cancer 4. Skin ageing/wrinkling
Choose the correct answer using the options given below.
expl: Due to ozone depletion, the harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun will directly strike the earth, which can cause several problems such as sunburn, cataract, skin cancer, skin ageing/ wrinkling, etc.

stem: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is related to—

options.label: a
options.text: Reduction in the use of fossil fuels

options.label: d
options.text: Reduction in emissions of greenhouse gases

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is related to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and stabilising the atmospheric concentration of greenhouse gases. It is noteworthy that CO also comes under greenhouse gases.

stem: Which country hosted the COP28 climate summit in 2023?
expl: COP28 was held from 30 November to 12 December 2023 in the United Arab Emirates (Dubai). COP30, the climate change summit, was held from 10 to 21 November 2025 in Belém (Brazil).

stem: In November 2024, where was the United Nations Climate Change Conference, 2024 to be held?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP29) was held in Baku, Azerbaijan, from 11 to 22 November 2024. COP30 was held in Belém (Brazil) from 10 to 21 November 2025.

stem: The much-discussed “Lisbon Declaration” is related to the conservation of which entity?
expl: The Lisbon Declaration is related to the conservation of oceans. It may be noted that in 2022, a five-day United Nations Ocean Conference was concluded, in which more than 150 countries collectively agreed to scale up science-based and innovative actions to address the marine emergency. The declaration, along with bold commitments from all sections of society—youth, civil society, businesses, and the scientific community—clearly demonstrates the centrality of a safe, healthy, and productive ocean for food security, livelihoods, and a secure planet. The conference was co-hosted by Portugal and Kenya. More than 100 countries joined the High Ambition Coalition for Nature and People, pledging to protect 30% of the world’s oceans by 2030.

stem: Recently, where was the fourth session of the United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA-4) held?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: The fourth session of the United Nations Environment Assembly was held in Nairobi (Kenya) from 11 to 15 March 2019. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the fifth session of the United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA-5) was held in two parts— First part (UNEA-5.1) – February 2021, Nairobi (Kenya), in virtual format. Second part (UNEA-5.2) – 28 February to 2 March 2022, Nairobi (Kenya). The fifth session of UNEA was held in Nairobi from 28 February to 2 March 2022 in a hybrid mode. The main theme of UNEA-5 was “Strengthening Actions for Nature to Achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.” The seventh session of the United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA-7) was held from 8 to 12 December 2025 at the headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) in Nairobi, Kenya.

stem: Which one of the following statements regarding COP- 28 is incorrect?

options.label: c
options.text: Approval of the operational policy of the Loss and Damage Fund

expl: COP-28 was held from 30 November to 13 December 2023 in Dubai (United Arab Emirates). During the conference, the operational policy of the Loss and Damage Fund was approved and the institutional arrangements for the operation of the Santiago Network were also approved. It was not held in Doha (Qatar); therefore, option (b) is incorrect. COP-30 was held in November 2025 in Belém, Brazil.

stem: The UN climate conference held in Baku in 2024 concluded with an agreement that:

options.label: a
options.text: Aims to ban fossil fuels globally by 2030

options.label: b
options.text: Calls on developed countries to provide at least $S00 billion annually to developing nations by 2030

options.label: c
options.text: Calls on developed countries to provide at least $300 billion annually to developing nations by 2035

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP29) was held in Baku, Azerbaijan, from 11 to 22 November 2024, where discussions mainly focused on climate finance. At the end of the conference, a new global climate-finance target was adopted. Under this, it was agreed to increase the earlier target of USD 100 billion per year (set at Copenhagen, 2009) for developing countries to at least USD 300 billion per year by 2035.

stem: Himalayan Brown Bear, Asian Wild Buffalo, Desert Fox are examples of which?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Himalayan Brown Bear (Ursus arctos), Asian Wild Buffalo (Bubalus bubalis), and Desert Fox (Vulpes bucopus) are examples of rare species. They are included in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

stem: The atmosphere receives its maximum energy from-

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The atmosphere receives its maximum energy from long-wave terrestrial radiation.

stem: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Renewable resources are those resources which are rapidly renewed or replenished. Some of them are inexhaustible and are not affected by human activities, such as solar energy, wind energy, etc. In contrast, non-renewable resources have limited reserves. After the reserves are exhausted, they take many years to be renewed or replenished. Coal, nuclear fuel, petroleum, and natural gas fall under this category.

stem: Fossil fuels are examples of which type of resources?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Fossil fuels are non-renewable fuels, which are likely to be exhausted in the near future. These include petroleum, natural gas, coal, etc.

stem:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I List-II (a) Perform, Achieve (1) Introduced in the Union and Trade (PAT) Budget for 2023-24 scheme (b) Mangrove Initiative (2) Aims to reduce emissions for Shoreline in energy-intensive Habitats & Tangible industries Incomes (MISHTI) (c) The Lifestyle for (3) Launched in 2019as a Environment (LiFE) national-level initiative (d) National Clean Air (4) strategy Launched at Programme (NCAP) COP26 in Glasgow in November 2021
Code: A B C D

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme was started in 2012. It is implemented by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power. The objective of this scheme is to reduce specific energy consumption (i.e., energy use per unit of output) for designated consumers in energy-intensive sectors. The Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes (MISHTI) was first presented in the Union Budget 2023-24. This initiative was started on 5 June 2023. Its objective is to restore and promote mangroves as a unique natural ecosystem, and to protect and enhance the sustainability of coastal habitats. On 1 November 2021, during the COP26 Conference in Glasgow (Scotland), Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented the concept of the Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) initiative. In January 2019, the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) was started by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change as a national-level strategy. The objective of this programme is to improve air quality in 130 cities of 24 States/Union Territories (non-attainment cities and cities with a population of more than one million).

stem: In mountainous regions, the maximum number of bird species live in which forest?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In mountainous regions, the maximum number of bird species live in pine forests. In India, a total of 1,358 species of birds are found under 26 orders and 114 families.

stem: It is advised not to sleep under a tree at night because trees—

options.label: a
options.text: Release a lesser amount of oxygen

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/more than one of the above

expl: During the day, in the presence of sunlight, plants absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen during respiration. But at night, exactly the opposite happens: they absorb oxygen and release carbon dioxide. Thus, at night the amount of carbon dioxide increases under trees and a feeling of suffocation is felt; therefore, one should not sleep under a tree at night.

stem: Which of the following is not a component of chlorophyll?

options.label: e
options.text: none of the above/more than one of the above

expl: Leaf-green or chlorophyll is a protein-containing complex chemical compound. This pigment is the reason for the green color of leaves. Magnesium is the major element of chlorophyll. Besides magnesium, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, and oxygen are also present in chlorophyll.

stem: Which metal ion is found in chlorophyll?
expl: Magnesium ion is found in chlorophyll. Chlorophyll is the green photosynthetic pigment present in plants. It initiates the process that converts light energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis.

stem: India’s national mammal is—
expl: India’s national animal is the tiger (scientific name—Panthera tigris), which is a mammal. Therefore, as per the question, option (d) is the correct answer. In view of the declining number of tigers, the Government of India started “Project Tiger” from April 1973. As of December 2025, a total of 58 tiger reserves have been established in India.

stem: What is “Greenpeace” (Harit Shanti)?

options.label: c
options.text: An international organization of environmental supporters

expl: “Greenpeace” is a group of environmental activists, which was established in 1971 to oppose nuclear weapons testing by the United States. The headquarters of “Greenpeace” is in Amsterdam (Netherlands).

stem: The approximate weight of an adult Indian elephant is—
expl: The weight of an adult Indian elephant is between 3,000 and 5,000 kilograms. The heaviest elephant so far is the African savanna elephant, whose weight is about 24,000 pounds (about 10,886 kg). An adult Indian elephant eats about 250 to 300 kilograms of fodder daily.

stem: The flightless bird found in New Zealand is—
expl: The bird found in New Zealand, the kiwi, cannot fly; however, it can run very fast.

stem: Which state government launched the State-Level Committee for Vulture Conservation (SLCVC) for vulture conservation, as proposed under the National Action Plan for vulture conservation in India?
expl: According to a report, between 1993 and 2003, the vulture population in India declined by about 96 percent. The central government decided to run two action plans for vulture conservation—first in 2006 and second during 2020–2025. Among the important action points of this nationwide action plan, one is the formation of state-level committees to save the critically endangered vulture population. Taking a step in this direction, the state of Tamil Nadu constituted a state-level committee in 2022 to establish an institutional framework for effective vulture conservation.

stem: India's first Dolphin Observatory is being built in:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: India’s first Dolphin Observatory is being built in Bihar. It is being established in Bhagalpur district of Bihar.

stem: To monitor the Arctic climate, which country launched its first satellite ‘Arktika-M’?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In February 2021, Russia launched its first satellite, Arktika-M, to monitor the Arctic climate and environment.

stem: . How many Indian beaches have been recommended for the Blue Flag Certification recently?
expl: At the time of the question, Blue Flag certification had been awarded to 8 beaches in India. At present, Blue Flag certification has been awarded to 18 beaches in India. Their names are—Shivrajpur (Gujarat), Ghoghla (Diu), Shriwardhan, Nagaon, Parnaka, Guhagar, Ladghar (Maharashtra), Golden (Odisha), Kasarkod, Padubidri (Karnataka), Rushikonda (Andhra Pradesh), Radhanagar (Andaman and Nicobar Islands), Kovalam (Tamil Nadu), Eden (Puducherry), Minicoy Thundi, Kadmat (Lakshadweep), Kappad, Chal (Kerala).

stem: In India the Temperate Forest Research center is in which city?
expl: For research on temperate forests in India, the (HFRI) Himalayan Forest Research Institute has been established at Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) under the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE).

stem: The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute is located at—
expl: The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) is located in Nagpur, Maharashtra.

stem: Where has the Gharial breeding centre been established in India?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Gharials have been declared extinct in Bhutan, Pakistan, and Myanmar. India and Nepal are making efforts for their rehabilitation. One such effort is the gharial breeding centre at Deori, near Morena (Madhya Pradesh).

stem: Earth Day, observed on 22 April, is related to—

options.label: a
options.text: The end day of the Second World War

options.label: b
options.text: Ban on nuclear weapons on planet Earth

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Earth Day is celebrated worldwide on 22 April to promote environmental awareness. It was started by American Senator Gaylord Nelson in 1970 as an environmental education initiative. The theme of Earth Day observed on 22 April 2025 was ‘Our Power, Our Planet’
